terms.definition: A seizure during pregnancy.
terms.name: Maternal seizure

terms.definition: A type of focal motor status epilepticus characterized by repeated motor, typically clonic events repeatedly affecting the same segments of the body with spread of clonic movements through contiguous body parts unilaterally, and repeating over a sufficiently prolonged period to reach a diagnosis of status epilepticus.
terms.name: Repeated focal motor seizures

terms.definition: A generalized motor seizure is a type of generalized-onset seizure with predominantly motor (involving musculature) signs. The motor event could consist of an increase (positive) or decrease (negative) in muscle contraction to produce a movement.
terms.name: Generalized-onset motor seizure

terms.comment: Non-motor terms correspond to the earliest prominent sign or symptom.
terms.definition: A type of focal-onset seizure characterized by non-motor signs or symptoms (or behavior arrest) as its initial semiological manifestation.
terms.name: Focal non-motor seizure

terms.definition: A focal non-motor seizure in which awareness is retained throughout the seizure.
terms.name: Focal aware non-motor seizure

terms.comment: In order to characterize focal cognitive seizures, specific testing may be required early during the seizure.
terms.definition: A focal cognitive seizure involves an alteration in a cognitive function (which can be a deficit or a positive phenomenon such as forced thought), which occurs at seizure onset. To be classified as a focal cognitive seizure, the change in cognitive function should be specific and out of proportion to other relatively unimpaired aspects of cognition, because all cognition is impaired in a focal impaired awareness seizure.
terms.name: Focal cognitive seizure

terms.definition: A focal aware cognitive seizure during which awareness is retained throughout the seizure.
terms.name: Focal aware cognitive seizure

terms.definition: An eyelid myoclonia seizure is a type of generalized myoclonic seizure which may or may not be associated with loss of awareness.
terms.name: Eyelid myoclonia seizure

terms.definition: A focal cognitive seizure with dyscalculia and or acalculia characterized by retained awareness throughout the seizure.
terms.name: Focal aware cognitive seizure with dyscalculia/acalculia

terms.comment: Dyscalculia / acalculia is difficulty completing or understanding mathematical calculation. This seizure type is seen in seizures involving the dominant hemisphere parieto-temporal lobe region.
terms.definition: A focal cognitive seizure characterized by dyscalculia / acalculia as the initial semiological manifestation.
terms.name: Focal cognitive seizure with dyscalculia/acalculia

terms.comment: Forced thinking is the presence of intrusive thoughts, ideas or crowding of thoughts. This is a rare seizure type, seen in mesial parietal, posterior parahippocampal and frontal lobe seizures.
terms.definition: A focal cognitive seizure characterized by forced thinking as the initial semiological manifestation.
terms.name: Focal cognitive seizure with forced thinking

terms.comment: Expressive dysphasia / aphasia is the inability to express one's thoughts despite being aware of what they wished to say because of a disorder of language rather than articulation.
terms.definition: A focal cognitive seizure characterized by expressive dysphasia / aphasia as the initial semiological manifestation.
terms.name: Focal cognitive seizure with expressive dysphasia/aphasia

terms.definition: A focal cognitive seizure with dysgraphia / agraphia characterized by retained awareness throughout the seizure.
terms.name: Focal aware cognitive seizure with dysgraphia/agraphia

terms.comment: Anomia is the inability to name objects despite knowing what they are.
terms.definition: A focal cognitive seizure characterized by anomia as the initial semiological manifestation.
terms.name: Focal cognitive seizure with anomia

terms.definition: A focal motor seizure with dysarthria / anarthria characterized by impaired awareness at some point during the seizure.
terms.name: Focal impaired awareness motor seizure with dysarthria/anarthria
synonyms: Focal motor impaired awareness seizure with dysarthria/anarthria

terms.comment: Version id defined as sustained, forced, involuntary turning of the eyes or head.
terms.definition: A focal motor seizure with version characterized by impaired awareness at some point during the seizure.
terms.name: Focal impaired awareness motor seizure with version
synonyms: Focal motor impaired awareness seizure with version

terms.definition: A type of focal motor seizure in which awareness is partially or fully impaired at some point during the seizure.
terms.name: Focal impaired awareness motor seizure

terms.comment: The abnormal movements of dystonia resulting from co-contraction of agonist and antagonist muscles differentiates these from tonic seizures, see focal tonic seizure.
terms.definition: A focal motor seizure in which the initial semiological manifestation is the sustained contraction of both agonist and antagonist muscles producing athetoid or twisting movements, which produces abnormal postures.
terms.name: Focal motor seizure with dystonia

terms.definition: A focal motor seizure with dystonia characterized by retained awareness throughout the seizure.
terms.name: Focal aware motor seizure with dystonia
synonyms: Focal motor aware seizure with dystonia

terms.definition: A focal hyperkinetic seizure in which awareness is partially or fully impaired at some point during the seizure.
terms.name: Focal impaired awareness hyperkinetic seizure

terms.definition: A focal atonic seizure in which awareness is partially or fully impaired at some point during the seizure.
terms.name: Focal impaired awareness atonic seizure

terms.definition: A focal tonic seizure in which awareness is partially or fully impaired at some point during the seizure.
terms.name: Focal impaired awareness tonic seizure

terms.comment: These seizures arise in mesial temporal networks, especially the amygdala. They can be distinguished from panic attacks, by the presence of impaired awareness, automatisms and other features of an epileptic seizure appearing in a stereotyped manner. They are also distinguished from a focal autonomic seizure with epigastric sensation, where the onset seizure feature is an autonomic epigastric sensation, and fear may be present as a secondary feature.
terms.definition: Focal emotional seizure with agitation is characterized by the presence of psychomotor agitation as an expressed or observed emotion, at the outset of the seizure. Because of the unpleasant nature of these seizures, patients may also have anticipatory anxiety about having seizures.
terms.name: Focal emotional seizure with agitation

terms.comment: This is a rare seizure type, seen in seizures arising in the anterior insular cortex.
terms.definition: Focal emotional seizure with pleasure is characterized by the presence of a positive emotional experience with pleasure, bliss, joy, enhanced personal well-being, heightened self-awareness or ecstasy.
terms.name: Focal emotional seizure with pleasure

terms.definition: A focal aware autonomic seizure has an initial manifestation pertaining to autonomic nervous system function, which may be objective (for example, pupillary dilation) or subjective (for example, nausea). As a type of focal aware seizure, awareness is retained throughout.
terms.name: Focal aware autonomic seizure
synonyms: Focal autonomic seizures without altered responsiveness
Localised autonomic seizures without altered responsiveness
Localized autonomic seizures without altered responsiveness
Partial autonomic seizures without altered responsiveness

terms.definition: A focal motor seizure with dysarthria / anarthria characterized by retained awareness throughout the seizure.
terms.name: Focal aware motor seizure with dysarthria/anarthria
synonyms: Focal motor aware seizure with dysarthria/anarthria

terms.definition: Focal emotional seizure with anxiety, fear or panic as an expressed or observed emotion at the outset of the seizure, in which awareness is retained throughout.
terms.name: Focal aware emotional seizure with fear/anxiety/panic

terms.comment: These seizures arise in mesial temporal networks, especially the amygdala. They can be distinguished from panic attacks, by the presence of impaired awareness, automatisms and other features of an epileptic seizure appearing in a stereotyped manner. They are also distinguished from a focal autonomic seizure with epigastric sensation, where the onset seizure feature is an autonomic epigastric sensation, and fear may be present as a secondary feature.
terms.definition: Focal emotional seizure with anxiety is characterized by the presence of anxiety, fear or panic as an expressed or observed emotion, at the outset of the seizure. Because of the unpleasant nature of these seizures, patients may also have anticipatory anxiety about having seizures.
terms.name: Focal emotional seizure with fear/anxiety/panic

terms.definition: Focal emotional seizure with paranoia in which awareness is retained throughout.
terms.name: Focal aware emotional seizure with paranoia

terms.definition: Focal emotional seizure with anger in which awareness is retained throughout.
terms.name: Focal aware emotional seizure with anger

terms.definition: Focal emotional seizure with paranoia is characterized by the presence of paranoia as an expressed or observed emotion at the outset of the seizure.
terms.name: Focal emotional seizure with paranoia

terms.comment: This seizure type localizes to prefrontal or mesial temporal regions of the brain.
terms.definition: Focal emotional seizure with anger is characterized by the presence of anger, as an expressed or observed emotion, at the outset of the seizure. It may be accompanied by aggressive behavior.
terms.name: Focal emotional seizure with anger

terms.definition: A focal emotional seizure during which awareness is retained throughout the seizure.
terms.name: Focal aware emotional seizure

terms.definition: Focal emotional seizure with pleasure in which awareness is partially or fully impaired at some point during the seizure.
terms.name: Focal impaired awareness emotional seizure with pleasure

terms.definition: Focal emotional seizure with paranoia in which awareness is partially or fully impaired at some point during the seizure.
terms.name: Focal impaired awareness emotional seizure with paranoia

terms.definition: Focal emotional seizure with laughing in which awareness is partially or fully impaired at some point during the seizure.
terms.name: Focal impaired awareness emotional seizure with laughing

terms.definition: Focal emotional seizure with anger in which awareness is partially or fully impaired at some point during the seizure.
terms.name: Focal impaired awareness emotional seizure with anger

terms.definition: Focal emotional seizure with agitation in which awareness is retained throughout.
terms.name: Focal aware emotional seizure with agitation

terms.definition: A focal emotional seizure in which awareness is partially or fully impaired at some point during the seizure.
terms.name: Focal impaired awareness emotional seizure

terms.definition: Focal emotional seizure with pleasure in which awareness is retained throughout.
terms.name: Focal aware emotional seizure with pleasure

terms.definition: Focal emotional seizure with laughing in which awareness is retained throughout.
terms.name: Focal aware emotional seizure with laughing

terms.definition: Focal emotional seizure with crying (dacrystic)in which awareness is retained throughout.
terms.name: Focal aware emotional seizure with crying

terms.definition: A focal autonomic seizure characterized by impaired awareness at some point within the seizure.
terms.name: Focal impaired awareness autonomic seizure
synonyms: Focal autonomic seizure with altered responsiveness
Localised autonomic seizure with altered responsiveness
Localized autonomic seizure with altered responsiveness
Partial autonomic seizure with altered responsiveness

terms.comment: These seizures involve the parietal cortex, temporo-parieto-occipital junction or parieto-temporal cortex.
terms.definition: A seizure characterized by symptoms of dizziness, spinning, vertigo or sense of rotation as its first clinical manifestation.
terms.name: Focal sensory seizure with vestibular features

terms.definition: Focal emotional seizure with anxiety, fear or panic as an expressed or observed emotion at the outset of the seizure, in which awareness is partially or fully impaired at some point during the seizure.
terms.name: Focal impaired awareness emotional seizure with fear/anxiety/panic

terms.definition: A focal emotional seizure with agitation in which awareness is partially or fully impaired at some point during the seizure.
terms.name: Focal impaired awareness emotional seizure with agitation

terms.definition: Focal emotional seizure with crying in which awareness is partially or fully impaired at some point during the seizure.
terms.name: Focal impaired awareness emotional seizure with crying

terms.definition: A focal cognitive seizure in which awareness is partially or fully impaired at some point during the seizure.
terms.name: Focal impaired awareness cognitive seizure

terms.definition: A focal hemiclonic seizure in which awareness is retained throughout.
terms.name: Focal aware hemiclonic seizure

terms.comment: A single or short cluster of brief muscle contractions (jerks), each jerk is typically milliseconds in duration.
terms.definition: A type of focal myoclonic seizure during which awareness is fully retained throughout.
terms.name: Focal aware myoclonic seizure
